narrator: Newspaper correspondent of The Dailygraph (pasted in Mina's journal); the captain of the Demeter (log); Mina Murray (journal)
dates: Log 6 July - 4 August; storm 6-7 August night; cutting 8-9 August; Mina 8 and 10 August
summary: A newspaper cutting describes a sudden, ferocious storm at Whitby after a beautiful day, ending with a Russian schooner, lashed to its helm by a dead man, driving into the harbour and grounding on Tate Hill Pier, from which an immense dog leaps ashore and vanishes. The ship is the Demeter of Varna, in ballast of silver sand with fifty-style great wooden boxes of mould consigned to solicitor Mr. S. F. Billington; a mastiff is found torn to pieces near the pier. The captain's log, recovered from a corked bottle, records a voyage from Varna in which crew vanish one by one, a tall thin pale stranger is glimpsed, the mate's knife passes through it, the mate opens a box and then leaps overboard, and the captain lashes himself to the wheel with a crucifix. The verdict is open and the captain is honoured with a grand funeral. Mina's journal records Lucy sleepwalking during the storm, the funeral, Mr. Swales found dead on the seat with a broken neck and terror on his face, and a dog that rages and then cowers on the suicide's tombstone.

scenes.title: The calm before the storm
scenes.location: Whitby, East Cliff churchyard and sea
scenes.summary: Mares'-tails appear in the sky; a flamboyant sunset gathers crowds on the cliff; the wind dies to a dead calm and boats stay in harbour. A foreign schooner under full sail idles at sea.
scenes.key_quote: As idle as a painted ship upon a painted ocean.

scenes.title: The tempest breaks
scenes.summary: A hollow booming, then the storm hits: giant waves overtop the piers, sea-fog rolls in, lightning flashes; the piers are cleared and the new East Cliff searchlight guides boats into harbour.
scenes.key_quote: The sea, running mountains high, threw skywards with each wave mighty masses of white foam.

scenes.title: The schooner enters the harbour
scenes.summary: Wind shifts to north-east and the schooner leaps between the piers, a corpse lashed to the helm, and drives onto Tate Hill Pier.
scenes.key_quote: lashed to the helm was a corpse, with drooping head, which swung horribly to and fro at each motion of the ship.

scenes.title: The dog leaps ashore
scenes.location: Tate Hill Pier and East Cliff
scenes.summary: As the keel touches sand an immense dog springs from below deck, leaps off the bow and bolts toward the churchyard cliff into the dark beyond the searchlight.
scenes.key_quote: an immense dog sprang up on deck from below, as if shot up by the concussion.

scenes.title: The coastguard and the dead steersman
scenes.location: Deck of the Demeter at Tate Hill Pier
scenes.summary: The coastguard recoils from the corpse; hands tied to a wheel spoke over a crucifix and beads, flesh cut to the bone; a doctor says dead two days; a corked bottle with a roll of paper is found in his pocket.
scenes.key_quote: Between the inner hand and the wood was a crucifix, the set of beads on which it was fastened being around both wrists and wheel.

scenes.title: Cargo and the dead mastiff
scenes.summary: The ship is the Demeter of Varna, ballast of silver sand and great wooden boxes of mould for Billington of 7 The Crescent. The dog has vanished; a coal merchant's half-bred mastiff is found with throat torn and belly slit.
scenes.key_quote: its throat was torn away, and its belly was slit open as if with a savage claw.

scenes.title: Log of the Demeter: departure to the Mediterranean
scenes.location: Aboard the Demeter: Varna, Bosphorus, Dardanelles, Cape Matapan
scenes.summary: Cargo of silver sand and earth boxes loaded; Turkish customs bribed; the crew grow scared and cross themselves; Petrofsky vanishes on watch.
scenes.key_quote: they only told him there was something, and crossed themselves.

scenes.title: The stranger sighted and the ship search
scenes.location: Aboard the Demeter, deck-house, hold with big boxes
scenes.summary: Olgaren sees a tall thin man on deck who vanishes; the whole crew searches with lanterns stem to stern and finds only the big boxes.
scenes.key_quote: he saw a tall, thin man, who was not like any of the crew, come up the companion-way, and go along the deck forward, and disappear.

scenes.title: Men disappear in Biscay and the Channel
scenes.location: Atlantic, Bay of Biscay, English Channel, fog
scenes.summary: Storm and fog; crewmen vanish after each watch (second mate, watch and steersman, more); the captain and mate arm themselves; a fog seems to move with the ship.
scenes.key_quote: There seems some doom over this ship.

scenes.title: The mate and the box
scenes.location: Hold and deck of the Demeter
scenes.summary: The mate stabs the pale tall figure but the knife passes through; he opens a box with a tool-chest, screams, sees It, and leaps into the sea.
scenes.key_quote: I saw It, like a man, tall and thin, and ghastly pale... I gave It my knife; but the knife went through It, empty as the air.

scenes.title: The captain ties himself to the wheel
scenes.summary: Alone, the captain sees Him, decides to lash his hands and a holy object to the wheel to save his soul, and writes the log into a bottle.
scenes.key_quote: I shall tie my hands to the wheel... and along with them I shall tie that which He—It!—dare not touch.

scenes.title: Verdict and public funeral planned
scenes.summary: An open verdict; the captain is a local hero, with a procession of over a hundred boats and burial in the cliff churchyard. The great dog is never found.
scenes.key_quote: The folk here hold almost universally that the captain is simply a hero.

scenes.title: Lucy sleepwalks in the storm
scenes.location: Mina and Lucy's room, the Crescent; Whitby harbour
scenes.summary: Lucy dresses twice in her sleep and Mina puts her back to bed; at dawn they see grim waves bullying through the harbour mouth.
scenes.key_quote: Lucy did not wake; but she got up twice and dressed herself.

scenes.title: Funeral, Swales's death, and the dog on the tombstone
scenes.summary: The captain is buried near Lucy's seat. Swales is found dead on the seat with neck broken and a look of horror. A dog howls and rages until thrown onto the tombstone, where it cowers in terror; Lucy is distressed.
scenes.key_quote: The moment it touched the stone the poor thing became quiet and fell all into a tremble.

locations.name: Whitby East Cliff churchyard
locations.description: Cliff-top graveyard commanding sea views; flat thruff-stones project over the lane where the cliff has fallen away; walk along the cliff; seat fixed on a tombstone.
features: flat tombstones overhanging the lane to East Pier
locations.quote: some of the flat tombstones... actually project over where the sustaining cliff has fallen away

locations.name: Tate Hill Pier
locations.description: Small pier in the south-east corner of the harbour under the East Cliff, with an accumulation of sand and gravel; the Demeter drives onto it.
locations.quote: pitched herself on that accumulation of sand and gravel washed by many tides and many storms

locations.name: Whitby harbour piers
locations.description: Two piers with lanterned lighthouses, iron stanchions, narrow mouth, East Pier and West Pier; Drawbridge links West Cliff.
locations.quote: the lanthorns of the lighthouses which rise from the end of either pier

locations.name: The Demeter (schooner)
locations.description: Russian schooner from Varna, crew of five hands plus captain; cargo of silver sand ballast and great wooden boxes of mould.
locations.quote: the schooner is a Russian from Varna, and is called the Demeter

locations.name: Whitby mortuary
locations.description: Place where the dead steersman is taken to await inquest.
locations.quote: placed in the mortuary to await inquest

characters.role: Writer of the log, hero of Whitby
characters.appearance: hands cut to the bone by cords after two days dead
notable_lines: I am captain, and I must not leave my ship.

characters.name: First mate
notable_lines: It is here; I know it, now.

characters.name: Crew of the Demeter
characters.role: Russian hands: Petrofsky, Abramoff, Olgaren, second mate, cook

characters.name: The Stranger / It
characters.role: Tall thin ghastly pale man on the ship
characters.appearance: tall, thin, ghastly pale, like a man

characters.name: Mr. S. F. Billington
characters.role: Whitby solicitor, consignee at 7 The Crescent

characters.name: Mr. Swales
characters.appearance: neck broken, look of fear and horror

objects.name: Crucifix and beads
objects.description: Crucifix on a string of beads wound around both of the dead captain's wrists and the wheel spoke.
objects.function_in_story: Held against It; protects his soul; dread of 'that which He dare not touch'.
objects.quote: Between the inner hand and the wood was a crucifix, the set of beads on which it was fastened being around both wrists and wheel

objects.name: Corked bottle with log addendum
objects.description: Carefully corked bottle holding a little roll of paper.
objects.quote: In his pocket was a bottle, carefully corked, empty save for a little roll of paper

objects.name: Log-book of the Demeter
objects.description: Ship's log in order until three days before landing.
objects.quote: the log-book of the Demeter, which was in order up to within three days

objects.name: Great wooden boxes of mould
objects.description: Big wooden boxes invoiced as clay, filled with earth; the only cargo besides silver sand ballast; one is unscrewed by the mate.
objects.quote: a number of great wooden boxes filled with mould

objects.name: Silver sand ballast
objects.description: Almost the entire cargo as ballast.
objects.quote: almost entirely in ballast of silver sand

objects.name: Searchlight
objects.description: New, untried searchlight on the East Cliff summit, swept across the sea.
objects.function_in_story: Guides boats and reveals the dead helmsman.
objects.quote: On the summit of the East Cliff the new searchlight was ready for experiment

objects.name: Mate's knife
objects.description: Knife used against the intangible figure.
objects.function_in_story: Passes through It; shows ordinary steel useless against it.
objects.quote: the knife went through It, empty as the air

objects.name: Tool-chest and lantern
objects.description: Mate carries them to unscrew the boxes.
objects.function_in_story: Opens the boxes in the hold.
objects.quote: I saw him come out on deck again with a tool-chest and a lantern

objects.name: Lanterns for the search
objects.description: Lanterns carried abreast by the crew.

objects.name: Handspike
objects.description: Wooden lever the mate would use to keep men in order.
objects.quote: he would engage to keep them out of trouble with a handspike

objects.name: Bible-less fog and wheel ropes
objects.description: Cords binding the captain's hands to the wheel, knots tied with teeth.
objects.quote: the man must have tied up his own hands, fastening the knots with his teeth

objects.name: Seat on the tombstone
objects.description: Seat fixed on the tombstone slab of the suicide's grave.
objects.function_in_story: Where Swales dies; dog cowers when thrown on the stone.
objects.quote: the tombstone on which the seat is fixed

creatures.name: The immense dog
creatures.description: Huge dog that springs from the hold on grounding and vanishes toward the churchyard; later a half-bred mastiff is killed in a fight with a savage opponent (implied the dog).
creatures.behaviour: Flees into darkness; savage killer with claw-like wounds on the mastiff.
creatures.quote: an immense dog sprang up on deck from below

creatures.name: The tall thin pale stranger (It / Him)
creatures.description: Tall, thin, ghastly pale figure that appears on the deck, bows, and in the hold; leaves no trace; intangible to a knife.
creatures.behaviour: Appears at night or fog, takes crew one by one from watch; fog seems to travel with the ship.
weaknesses: fears a crucifix (inferred: captain ties 'that which He dare not touch' to his hands)
creatures.quote: tall and thin, and ghastly pale

creatures.name: Terrified dog at the grave
creatures.description: Master's dog, furious and then cowering on the suicide's tombstone.
creatures.behaviour: Barks and howls with bristling hair, quiets in terror on the stone.
creatures.quote: in such a pitiable state of terror

creatures.name: Sea-fog
creatures.description: White wet clouds that seem like the hands of drowned dead.
creatures.behaviour: Sweeps in ghostly fashion; seems to follow the Demeter.
creatures.quote: the spirits of those lost at sea were touching their living brethren with the clammy hands of death

vampire_lore.rule: Dracula travels in boxes of his native earth
vampire_lore.detail: The only cargo is great wooden boxes of mould, hidden in the hold, labelled clay.
vampire_lore.quote: a number of great wooden boxes filled with mould

vampire_lore.rule: Ordinary weapons pass through his shape
vampire_lore.detail: The mate's knife goes through It, 'empty as the air'.
vampire_lore.quote: the knife went through It, empty as the air

vampire_lore.detail: The captain ties a crucifix with his hands to the wheel to keep It from touching him.

vampire_lore.rule: Appears and vanishes through closed hatchways
vampire_lore.detail: The stranger leaves the deck with all hatches closed.

vampire_lore.rule: Controls weather: fog and storm accompany him
vampire_lore.detail: Fog moves with the ship; storm rises as it nears England.
vampire_lore.quote: the fog, which seems to move with us

vampire_lore.rule: Takes the form of an immense dog
vampire_lore.detail: A large dog leaps from the ship on landing and vanishes; the mastiff is torn (inferred identification).
vampire_lore.quote: an immense dog sprang up on deck

vampire_lore.rule: Kills his victims from the crew one per night
vampire_lore.detail: A man is lost after each watch, with no struggle recorded.
vampire_lore.quote: Like the first, he came off his watch and was not seen again.

vampire_lore.rule: Animals fear the suicide's grave / sense evil
vampire_lore.detail: The dog rages at the grave seat, then cowers when placed on the tombstone.
vampire_lore.quote: it became quiet and fell all into a tremble

vampire_lore.rule: Running water crossing at the harbour mouth
vampire_lore.detail: The ship only enters port when the wind shifts and drives it; the fog melts exactly then (weak inference, unstated).
vampire_lore.quote: the remnant of the sea-fog melted in the blast

puzzles.name: Searching the ship
puzzles.setup: Crew believes a stranger is aboard.
puzzles.obstacle: A hidden presence with no hiding places except big boxes.
puzzles.book_solution: Whole crew with lanterns search stem to stern; find only the boxes.
puzzles.game_idea: Sweep-search puzzle on a ship cross-section: track light radius, mark rooms cleared and note which boxes cannot be opened yet.
puzzles.quote: we left no corner unsearched. As there were only the big wooden boxes

puzzles.name: Reading the weather
puzzles.setup: Mares'-tails, sunset colours and dead calm.
puzzles.obstacle: Predict the storm to protect boats.
puzzles.book_solution: An old fisherman and the coastguard read the signs and warn captains.
puzzles.game_idea: Observation puzzle: match sky signs to forecast and decide which boats to hold in harbour.
puzzles.quote: a sudden show of 'mares'-tails' high in the sky to the north-west

puzzles.name: Searchlight rescue
puzzles.setup: Boats run for harbour in tempest and fog.
puzzles.obstacle: Guide each boat past the piers.
puzzles.book_solution: The new searchlight sweeps the surface and lights the harbour mouth.
puzzles.game_idea: Real-time sweep mini-game: aim a searchlight beam to mark rocks and entrances as boats approach.
puzzles.quote: able, by the guidance of the sheltering light, to avoid the danger of dashing against the piers.

puzzles.name: The captain's last log
puzzles.setup: Corpse tied to wheel with bottle in pocket.
puzzles.book_solution: Inquest reads the log and bottle paper; verdict open.
puzzles.game_idea: Forensic reconstruction: sort dated entries, match vanished crew to times and bind the mystery into a timeline.
puzzles.quote: Of course the verdict was an open one. There is no evidence to adduce.

puzzles.name: The box in the hold
puzzles.setup: Mate says It is in a box.
puzzles.book_solution: Mate unscrews one with a tool-chest and flees screaming.
puzzles.game_idea: Risky unscrew puzzle: choose which box to open under time pressure; one holds the creature's earth.
puzzles.quote: I'll unscrew them one by one and see.

combat.name: Mate stabs the stranger
combat.tactics: Mate creeps behind the figure at the bows and stabs.
combat.outcome: Knife passes through It; no damage; mate goes mad.
combat.game_idea: Scripted fail encounter teaching that normal weapons do nothing; unlock crucifix or sacred items to inflict damage.
combat.quote: I crept behind It, and gave It my knife; but the knife went through It, empty as the air.

combat.name: The armed watch
combat.tactics: Go armed and wait for any sign of cause.
combat.outcome: Men keep vanishing; no fight happens.
combat.game_idea: Survival-horror night watch: stand watch in pairs in the fog; choose positions each turn while enemy picks off the weakest crew member.
combat.quote: Mate and I agreed to go armed henceforth and wait for any sign of cause.

combat.name: Mastiff vs the great dog
combat.tactics: Attack in the road near the pier.
combat.outcome: Mastiff killed, throat torn, belly slit.
combat.game_idea: Boss-intro cutscene or a defend-the-pier encounter against a huge dog form.
combat.quote: its throat was torn away, and its belly was slit open as if with a savage claw.

crafting.method: Tie hands one over the other to a wheel spoke with the crucifix between hand and wood, knots fastened with teeth.
crafting.purpose: Hold the wheel and hold the vampire at bay.
crafting.quote: Between the inner hand and the wood was a crucifix

dialogue_samples.line: She must fetch up somewhere, if it was only in hell.
dialogue_samples.context: Watching the schooner speed toward the reef.

dialogue_samples.speaker: First mate
dialogue_samples.line: It is in the hold, perhaps in one of those boxes. I'll unscrew them one by one and see.

dialogue_samples.speaker: First mate
dialogue_samples.line: The sea will save me from Him, and it is all that is left!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Captain

asset_candidates.name: Dead steersman at the wheel
asset_candidates.visual_description: Corpse slumped at the wheel with hands tied over a spoke by cords, crucifix on bead string between hand and wood, cut wrists.

asset_candidates.name: Crucifix on rosary beads
asset_candidates.visual_description: Small wooden or metal crucifix on a string of dark beads.

asset_candidates.name: Tate Hill Pier and sand heap
asset_candidates.visual_description: Short stone jetty under the cliff with a mound of sand and gravel in the corner.

asset_candidates.name: Whitby searchlight

asset_candidates.name: Giant black dog

asset_candidates.name: Storm sea and fog

quest_hooks: Survive the storm night: guide boats with the searchlight and clear the piers.
Board the Demeter: examine the dead helmsman, the bottle log and the crates before officials seal the ship.
Track the great dog from Tate Hill Pier up to the churchyard.
Investigate where the earth boxes were delivered (solicitor Billington, 7 The Crescent).
Watch over Lucy during the storm night and prevent her from leaving.
Find out why Swales died on the seat.
